description: A head selected on its own receives a raised head while the phrase that head leaves still waits as its own workspace. Stage 6 selects the silent Foc head beside the finite clause mTP, completed one stage earlier; its T-to-Foc head movement then builds the landing mFocComplex from the raised mTComplex and mFocHead and attaches mTP below the new mFocCore. The layout kept mTP at its earlier-stage place, laid the new head out at its final place far to its right, and at the movement moved the whole clause across to it (a median 5,900 layout units; a 539 px first-paint jump at 1440×900). mTP now keeps its place through that moment; the selected head stands beside the head that joins it and only makes room for it.
source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning effort, Codex OAuth qualification run, 26 Oct 2026 (sol-parts-20261026, n4-29-hu-long-focus, analysis 0; ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/sol-parts-20261026/runs), read with the Oct 27 ship candidate's intake. Intentional variant: the relative clause amelyet Péter ajánlott, the four stages that build it and the relative-modification relation of the book expression are removed; every other stage keeps the model's nodes, relations and text. The sentence is the remaining words.
sentence: Tegnap a könyvet csak Mari olvasta el az egész osztályból.

derivationStages.statement: Construct the definite book expression with its relative modifier.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Adjoin the completed relative clause to the nominal projection containing könyvet, then merge the definite article a. The relative operator is interpreted as ranging over the book denoted by this nominal, with its lower occurrence supplying the object of Péter's recommendation. The resulting definite nominal bears accusative morphology and will enter the main clause as its object. The suffix on könyvet remains part of the lexical word.

derivationStages.statement: Merge the book expression as the main verb's object.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge olvasta with the complete definite book expression. The object receives the Theme role of reading. Olvasta is introduced in its surface past-tense, third-person singular definite-conjugation form; later agreement will license that form without adding separately pronounced inflectional terminals.

derivationStages.statement: Introduce el, the focused subject, and the class-domain restrictor.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Build a predicational layer with el in its preverbal modifier position and the reading predicate below it. Merge transitive v and introduce the constituent csak Mari as its external argument; Mari receives the Agent role through this constituent. Transitive v licenses the book expression's accusative Case. Build az egész osztályból as an elative nominal and right-adjoin it to the v projection. This adjunct supplies the class-based comparison domain for the subject alternatives, rather than a source argument of reading. The elative suffix remains within osztályból. The particle csak associates with Mari inside the constituent that will move to the focus position.

derivationStages.statement: Raise the main verb to v while leaving el in the predicational layer.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Raise olvasta from its previously established V position to transitive v and leave a silent V trace. The particle el does not accompany this head movement: it remains in the modifier position above the lexical predicate. This separation is necessary for the verb–particle order that the preverbal focus will require.

derivationStages.statement: Establish main-clause finiteness and definite conjugation.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge past finite T and raise the existing v–verb complex to T, leaving a silent v trace. T agrees with Mari and licenses nominative Case on the subject constituent without first moving that constituent into a separate preverbal subject position. The definite book object licenses the definite conjugation realized by olvasta. The subject remains in its established external-argument position until focus movement.

derivationStages.statement: Derive the immediately preverbal exclusive focus csak Mari.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge Foc above the finite clause. First raise the existing T–verb complex to Foc, leaving a silent T trace. Then internally merge the complete constituent csak Mari in the focus specifier from its external-argument position, leaving a silent nominal trace. The exclusive particle takes the reading predicate as its scope and excludes the other contextually relevant members of the whole class. Because el stays below the raised finite verb, this produces csak Mari olvasta el rather than a preverbal el sequence.

values.interpretation: Mari, and no other relevant member of the whole class, read the book

derivationStages.statement: Front the complete book expression as the main-clause topic.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge Top above the focus projection and internally merge the definite book expression in its specifier, replacing its established object position with a silent trace. The relative clause moves with the nominal because it is contained within that nominal's projection. The fronted expression is interpreted as the aboutness topic of the proposition whose subject focus is csak Mari; it is not a second focus.

values.interpretation: the book is the entity about which the focused proposition is asserted

derivationStages.statement: Complete the declarative with the initial temporal frame tegnap.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a temporal Frame projection above the object topic and introduce tegnap in its specifier. Tegnap restricts the main reading event to yesterday; it does not independently require Péter's recommendation to have occurred yesterday. Finally merge a silent declarative C. With silent traces and functional heads unpronounced, the completed tree yields Tegnap a könyvet, amelyet Péter ajánlott, csak Mari olvasta el az egész osztályból. The initial temporal frame, object topic, exclusive subject focus, postverbal particle, and final class-domain adjunct thus have distinct structural positions.
